prompt: Vertical 9:16 photograph on 35 mm film with a long telephoto lens from across a rain-soaked London junction at night, compressing the street so that the front three-quarters of a red double-decker bus, waiting at the lights, stands tall in the middle of the frame. Its whole upper-deck side carries a long printed campaign advert: at the front end, where the advert drops down beside the door, a large retouched campaign photograph of the man from the reference image, holding a phone to his right ear with his right hand, brows lifted, a wide salesman's smile, eyes to camera; running along the upper deck beside his face, in enormous heavy black sans-serif capitals on a clean white strip, the words "SAVE OUR NHS", each letter taller than the upper-deck windows are wide, sharp and perfectly spelled, no other text, no logo. Light sources: a row of sodium-orange street lamps behind the bus, the bus's own warm lit windows, the red of a traffic light reflected on the wet road, and in the out-of-focus foreground a flare of blue emergency light from a held ambulance, its light bouncing off the bus's wet paintwork and the white advert. Rain streaks visible against the lamps, the tarmac a mirror of orange, red and blue, cold teal shadows between the buildings, heavy film grain, halation round every light. The bus's destination display is dark and unreadable; no route numbers, no number plates, no shop signs: the slogan is the only readable text in the frame. Thanks.
